name: salamander-g3-jumping-uppercut
character: The salamander gunslinger (55 joints: a Humanoid body with Mixamo names; each hand has a thumb and THREE fingers (Thumb, Index, Middle, Ring chains), no little finger; five tail joints Tail1-Tail5 under Hips; three rigid joints under Head: Hat (his sombrero, its own mesh), Mustache (the fake mustache on his snout) and Straw (a wheat straw in the left corner of his mouth)). He is lanky: in the rig his hip joints stand 0.42 m above the floor when straight, thigh 0.176 m, shin 0.137 m, upper arm 0.158 m, forearm 0.093 m, long hands (about 0.15 m wrist to fingertip); 0.95 m to the top of his head, 1.13 m with the hat (the game draws him 1.8 times bigger). A thick tail hangs behind him from the seat of his jeans. His poncho is cloth simulated in the game and is not in this rig: pose the body only.
image_notes: 1: the salamander model with his arms down (front, three-quarter, side). His poncho is not in the rig.
notes: Salamander ground.3 (anim.salamander.g3): Jumping Uppercut, his launcher. Replaces the first Uppercut (owner 2026-10-28: "too simple and confusing", every attack "too fast"). Authored slow at 84 ticks; the game sets the final speed.
description:
The salamander's ground.3, Jumping Uppercut: his launcher. A big, wound-up saloon-brawl uppercut: he sinks deep, then springs off the floor driving his right fist up past his face, high over his sombrero, and lands heavily.

Who he is. A tiger salamander (image 1): olive-black skin with yellow blotches, a smirk, a fake handlebar mustache, a straw in his mouth, a wide brown sombrero, a rust-orange poncho, faded patched jeans with his tail out through the seat patch, brown boots with star spurs. He is the Wannabe Legend: a make-believe gunslinger who plays every Western cliche with total conviction. His finger guns belong to his specials only. His normals are plain, scrappy saloon-brawl hits with his own body: no finger guns, no props, open or loosely closed hands. One clear idea per move, performed with his whole body and given time to develop: a real anticipation, weight shifts and steps, the hit carried through the hips and shoulders, a follow-through that carries him off balance, and a cocky settle. The game speeds the clip up to the move's length, so never rush a beat: the owner's note on every earlier attack was "too fast, too simple".

How the game plays it. The match camera sits straight behind him, so the action must read from behind: arms out to the side or up, not hidden in front of the chest. The fighter does not travel in the clip unless said; the game moves him. The game crossfades in and out over about 0.1 s.

The floor. It is at up = -0.396 m in this character frame (origin: the hips of his idle at tick 0). With a flat boot the toe joint (ToeBase) sits about 0.008 m above the floor and the ankle (Foot) about 0.078 m above it. Standing straight his hip joint is 0.42 m above the floor. Never push a boot through the floor.

His idle, where ground moves start and end (reference `showdown`, the entry pose): the showdown stance, boots planted wide, knees bent, hands hovering out at his hips over invisible holsters, facing front.

The move (84 ticks, played once; the game may speed it up):
- Tick 0: the showdown stance.
- Tick 12, sinking: knees bend, hips drop, the chest leans forward and turns 25-35 degrees to his right; the right fist (loosely closed) swings down and back beside his right hip; the left fist comes up to guard his chin.
- Tick 22, coiled: the deepest point. Hips 10-14 cm below the stance, the right fist low behind his right hip near the knee, chin tucked, the tail curled low along the floor, the hat brim dipped forward.
- Tick 30, launch: legs drive straight, heels peel off the floor, the chest turns back through front; the fist swings in to his centre line and rises in front of his chest.
- Tick 33, contact: both boots leave the floor (toes 4-8 cm up), body stretched tall. The right fist drives straight up HIS CENTRE LINE, in front of his face and out past the front of the hat brim, finishing above the brim at the height of the crown or higher, arm angled up and forward (not straight up beside his head). The hit must land on an opponent standing straight in front of him, not to his right: the fist is centred on his nose line, not out over his right shoulder. The brim is 0.58 m wide (0.29 m to each side of his head and about 0.29 m ahead of the crown): the fist and forearm pass in front of the brim's front edge, never through it, so from behind the fist pops up over the middle of the sombrero. Chin up, following the fist. The left fist pulls down to his left hip. The rush tips the hat back on his head and it wobbles; the tail whips up behind him.
- Ticks 33-40, the hang: at the top, a moving hold; the feet peak about tick 36.
- Tick 44, landing: both boots land together, wide, knees give deep (hips 5-8 cm below the stance), the fist still above his head but coming down; the hat flops forward.
- Tick 52: he rises out of the landing as the right arm comes straight down in front of him to his right side (no swing round).
- Tick 58, recovered (he can act).
- Ticks 58-84: he settles into the stance and the hands settle over the holsters. After the hit he just recovers: no gesture, flourish or arm business in the ending lag (owner 2026-10-28: "normals don't need to have personality in ending lag"); the arms take the shortest calm path back to the holsters while the body regains its balance.
- Tick 84: the showdown stance again, matching tick 0.
No boot slides on the floor: a boot is either planted or in the air.
- Life. Overlap everything: the hips lead, the chest follows 1-2 ticks later, the arms and head trail 2-3 ticks, the tail and the hat (joint Hat, a few degrees at most) trail the most. No two parts stop on the same tick, and every hold is a moving hold (key its end 2-5 degrees on from its start). Use the follow-through helpers from the guide's Life and Flow sections. Treat every flow or life warning as a failure.
